chunks: Say: 'God has veritably spoken the truth. So now follow the way of Abraham the upright, who was not of idolaters.'

key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abraham (peace be upon him), the patriarch of monotheism
key_terms.الْمُشْرِكِينَ: Idolaters/Those who associate partners with God
key_terms.حَنِيفًا: Upright/Monotheist, referring to one who turns away from idolatry

ai.seo_question: Who is the model of pure monotheism that believers are commanded to follow according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to validate the continuity of the prophetic message, positioning Abraham not merely as a patriarch but as the archetype of *Hanifiyyah* (pure monotheism) free from later sectarian innovations. It underscores the Shia emphasis on returning to the primordial faith (*Fitrah*) as exemplified by the Ahl al-Bayt, who preserve the true essence of Abraham's legacy against the distortions of polytheism (*Shirk*).
